title: Youmu: Efficient Columnar Data Pipeline for LLM Training
problem: LLM training datasets stored in columnar formats (Parquet) must be converted to other formats before training, wasting terabytes of storage. Direct use of columnar data causes 100x+ efficiency drops due to granularity mismatch between coarse columnar chunk I/O (100s of MB) and fine-grained random access needed for shuffling.
motivation: Parquet-to-JSON conversion for 43 TB FineWeb costs ~95 TB extra storage. Existing solutions either cache entire datasets in DRAM (high memory), use memory-mapped I/O (cache thrashing), or sacrifice shuffle quality (streaming). A solution that eliminates format conversion while preserving shuffle quality and GPU utilization is needed.
method: Youmu breaks data into small chunks called pages (kilobytes to megabytes) instead of huge blocks, and at startup builds an index from Parquet file metadata; when training needs a random page, layered binary search (a fast multi-level lookup) finds its exact location on disk. The system reads compressed pages directly from SSDs and decodes them using metadata, avoiding the need to load everything into memory first. It feeds pages into a fixed-size buffer that continuously shuffles data as it's consumed, maintaining high randomization for training. The implementation is about 500 lines of Rust with Python bindings.
key_novelty: Youmu's core idea is using small pages (kilobytes to megabytes) as the unit of direct access to Parquet columnar data, eliminating format conversion while enabling global shuffling across billions of pages in terabyte-scale datasets.
contributions: Identification of granularity mismatch as the root cause of columnar data inefficiency for training
Global page index with layered binary search for O(log n) random page access across TB-scale datasets
Page-level direct I/O avoiding columnar chunk overhead and unused column reads
Aggressive buffer shuffle providing superior shuffle quality over streaming baselines
~80% less memory footprint vs distributed memory-based solutions (30-47 GB vs 100-150 GB per node)
Comparable throughput to Ray Data with much lower memory (3ms batch latency for page shuffle)
Perplexity improvement of 0.3-0.7 over local shuffle for LLM pre-training
Rust implementation with PyArrow-compatible Python APIs

metrics.memory_footprint_reduction: ~80% vs distributed memory-based (30-47 GB vs 100-150 GB per node)
metrics.batch_latency: 3ms for page shuffle, 0.4s for full random shuffle
metrics.shuffle_quality: 10.6% of no-shuffle degradation vs 53.3% for streaming
metrics.shuffle_wall_time: <10 seconds initialization vs 1000s+ for Ray Data
metrics.disk_usage: No additional disk vs 2.6 TB for HuggingFace Feather conversion

baselines: Ray Data (distributed memory, full and chunk shuffle)
limitations: Targets SSD-backed storage systems; benefits depend on storage performance; page-level granularity introduces some I/O waste for fully random shuffle; primarily validated for auto-regressive pre-training (single-column datasets); metadata caching requires 30-47 GB per node.
primary_theme: LLM Training Data Pipeline / Columnar I/O Optimization
